100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On July 27, 1926, the United Kingdom faced mounting tensions as labor strikes continued to disrupt industries, particularly coal mining, leading to widespread unrest. In Germany, the government struggled to stabilize the economy amid hyperinflation, sparking fears of social upheaval. Meanwhile, in the United States, summer heatwaves persisted, prompting concerns over public health and agricultural impacts across the Midwest.
